clue.text: Minister first to advise Mrs May about makeover

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the word advise
about asks for the title of Mrs May to be turned round

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister, abbreviated PM

explanation.surface: A government minister advising Theresa May on giving her image a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May's job was Prime Minister; 'about' turns its abbreviation round, so the solver must think of her title rather than her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a renovation or overhaul that gives something a fresh appearance.

clue.text: Portrait painter only bothered with warm colours for skin

indicators.note: for skin means the warm colours wrap around the other letters like a skin

parts.note: reds are warm colours on the palette

indicators.note: bothered suggests the word only is flustered and jumbled

explanation.surface: A portrait painter who only cares about warm flesh tones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' scrambles the word 'only'; 'for skin' makes the warm colours an outer layer round those jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was the leading eighteenth-century English portraitist and first president of the Royal Academy.

clue.text: Large Starbucks coffee too long arriving is cool

parts.note: venti is the Starbucks name for its large cup size
someone who takes too long to arrive is late

explanation.surface: A big coffee order arrives so slowly it has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTI is Italian for twenty, the ounces in Starbucks' large size.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate a room is to let air through and so cool it; the verb senses match.

clue.text: Look unpleasant when caught

indicators.note: caught here means heard by the ear, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: a mean person is unpleasant

explanation.surface: Someone looks nasty when caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when caught' signals a sound-alike: MEAN said aloud gives the spelling MIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mien is a person's bearing or expression, the look they wear.

clue.text: Hard border dispute that divides the country

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an edge is a border
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A tough border dispute splitting a nation, like a hard Brexit border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' means countryside, not nation: a hedge row divides fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of shrubs and trees separate the fields across the British countryside.

clue.text: Risk is fair, I agree

parts.note: an expo is a trade fair or exhibition
saying sure means I agree

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing that a risk is reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure to danger is being at risk of it; both nouns name vulnerability.

clue.text: Ignored left and right, nothing earl ever says sticks

indicators.note: dropping letters at both the left and right ends of the phrase leaves a run of letters from within it

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's empty talk being ignored by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignored left and right' cuts the ends from 'nothing earl ever says', leaving the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear sticks in a car are also called gear levers.

clue.text: Ten to three, perhaps time I sweep up outside

indicators.note: outside means the turned word goes around the other letters
in a down clue, up asks for the letters to be read bottom to top

parts.note: a sweep is a long oar

explanation.surface: At ten to three someone sweeps up outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OAR to RAO; 'outside' puts it round T and I. 'Ten to three' is not a clock time but 10:3.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten to three, written 10:3, is an example of a proportion between two numbers.

clue.text: Faction admits Irish connections

indicators.note: admits means lets the other letters in

parts.note: a wing of a party is a faction

explanation.surface: A political faction lets in people with Irish connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical wiring is the set of connections between components.

clue.text: When alfresco meal's half eaten clear food

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: half eaten means only half of the meal word remains

parts.note: a picnic is a meal eaten in the open air

explanation.surface: Someone clears away food once an outdoor meal is half gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half eaten' keeps PIC, the first half of PICNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a transparent savoury jelly, so a clear food.

clue.text: Harry Kane limited by OK team playing hardball

indicators.note: limited by means held within the other word

parts.note: yes means OK

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the name Kane is roughed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: England striker Harry Kane joining an OK side playing tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is a verb, not the footballer's first name: it roughs up the surname, and 'limited by' holds the result inside the word for OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Yankees play baseball, which uses a hard ball, so the phrase also puns on tough tactics.

clue.text: Man preparing to paper holds length to cover the wall

indicators.note: holds means contains the next letter

parts.note: a paster is someone applying paste before hanging paper

explanation.surface: A decorator gets a roll of paper ready to hang on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To plaster is to coat a wall with a smooth layer of render.

clue.text: Working in front of computers getting the job done

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: Someone at a computer screen finishing a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are on it means you are handling the task right now.

clue.text: Hollywood resolved 'listen to women', but only outwardly?

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and reformed, so the letters of listen are rearranged
only outwardly keeps just the outside letters of women

explanation.surface: Hollywood vows to listen to women but only for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' scrambles LISTEN to TINSEL; 'only outwardly' takes WN from WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, mocking its glitzy surface.

clue.text: Unreliable way to get to Heathrow first thing?

definitions.meaning: describing someone shifty who cannot be trusted

definitions.text: way to get to Heathrow first thing?
definitions.meaning: taking an overnight plane lands you at the airport early in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow is London's main airport; the second reading is a literal overnight flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night firm is untrustworthy; flying by night gets you to the airport at dawn.

clue.text: Date before breakfast, maybe at great cost

parts.note: before breakfast is one example of early in the day

explanation.surface: An early-morning date proves expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying dearly means paying a heavy price.

clue.text: Come up with a positive challenge to get daughter involved

parts.note: a pro is a positive point, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: involved means the daughter goes inside

parts.note: to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: A parent finds an upbeat activity to engage their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is to supply or produce it.

clue.text: Quite blue on the Conservative side

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down
conservatives sit on the political right

explanation.surface: Someone fairly true-blue, leaning Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative Party's colour, so the surface reads as politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright and quite both mean thoroughly or utterly, as in downright rude.

clue.text: Withholding affection if rude or misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests the letters of if rude or are out of order

explanation.surface: A parent withholds affection if a child is rude or naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Froideur, from French, means coldness or aloofness in manner.

clue.text: Say, less than complete absence of imperfection?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: something less than complete is not whole

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether being less than complete means lacking flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals that NOT WHOLE, spoken, gives the spelling with a silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a flaw in timber; when it drops out it leaves a hole, literally an absence of the flaw.

clue.text: Bronwen possibly one whose gender you're unsure of

definitions.text: one whose gender you're unsure of

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the name could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone called Bronwen is male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles BRONWEN, a Welsh girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby just born may have a gender not yet known to strangers, a playful description of an infant.

clue.text: Start earlier if picture is unfinished

indicators.note: is unfinished means the last letter of the picture word is dropped

parts.note: a drawing is a picture

explanation.surface: Begin sooner if the painting isn't done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unfinished' removes the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: When nights draw in, darkness arrives earlier in the evening as autumn advances.

clue.text: Animal you finally brought inside barking again …

indicators.note: brought inside means placed within the scrambled letters
barking means mad, so the letters of again go wild
finally picks the last letter of you

explanation.surface: An animal you finally bring indoors starts barking again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' scrambles AGAIN to IGANA; 'brought inside' adds U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard, an example of an animal.

clue.text: … for each person going down the road

parts.note: a means per or for each, as in once a day
a head is one person, as in so much a head

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the animal is brought in for each person heading down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means further on, the direction you travel when going along a road.

clue.text: Go easy on a politician trying to save the world

indicators.note: on places the easy word after the politician word

parts.words: a politician trying to save the world
parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmental party
a light task is easy

explanation.surface: Advice to go gently on an environmental campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a placement signal: the easy word sits after the politician, though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A green light is permission to proceed; giving it says go.

clue.text: Eleven minus three divided by eleven, one away

indicators.note: divided by means split apart by the other piece placed in the middle
minus three means the final three letters of the word are removed

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle with eleven, three and one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus three' cuts VEN to leave ELE; 'divided by' splits it with XI.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished from home, someone living away.

clue.text: British males' preparation for sex is rather dry

parts.note: the rut is the mating season when male deer compete

explanation.surface: A wry remark that British men's approach to romance is rather dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut on a champagne label means very dry, with little sugar.

clue.text: Bolt's quick, finishing sooner than expected

indicators.note: finishing sooner means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: fleet means swift or quick

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt is fast and finishes races early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing sooner than expected' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run away, to escape in a hurry.

clue.text: Feeling sparks by the fireplace

parts.note: at means by, as in at the door
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth

explanation.surface: Romance kindling beside the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling with excitement, like feeling electric sparks.

clue.text: Minimal legroom restricts movement

indicators.note: restricts means the letters are confined within these words

explanation.surface: Cramped airline seats limit how much passengers can move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' means a section of a symphony, not physical motion.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegro is a brisk section of a musical work, commonly a symphony's first part.

clue.text: Fresh water in Yorkshire? Start with a hole

indicators.note: start with puts the single letter a at the front

parts.note: pert means cheeky or fresh
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about clean water in Yorkshire and digging a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, flowing through Wensleydale; 'Fresh' means cheeky here.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or gap, the same as a hole.

clue.text: Lie protected huge corporation

definitions.meaning: to lie snugly sheltered, cuddled up
the Swiss food giant famous for coffee and chocolate

explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly; Nestlé is the multinational food company.
